papers.title: SEA-VQA: Southeast Asian Cultural Context Dataset For Visual Question Answering

coauthors.name: Peerat Limkonchotiwat
coauthors.affiliation: Vidyasirimedhi Institute of Science and Technology (VISTEC) at the time of SEA-VQA; now AI Singapore
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author of SEA-VQA, a 'Southeast Asian Cultural Context Dataset For Visual Question Answering', and a listed author of SEA-VL (arXiv 2503.07920), 'Crowdsource, Crawl, or Generate? Creating SEA-VL, a Multicultural Vision-Language Dataset for Southeast Asia', whose stated motivation is that advances 'often disproportionately benefit certain languages and cultures ... leaving underrepresented cultures - particularly those of Southeast Asia (SEA) - largely overlooked' and that the resource gap 'risks cultural irrelevance or bias against SEA populations'. Independent, repeated work on cultural representation and cultural bias in LLM/VLM benchmarks, not just co-authorship with the target.

coauthors.name: Sarana Nutanong
coauthors.affiliation: Vidyasirimedhi Institute of Science and Technology (VISTEC), Thailand
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Senior co-author of SEA-VQA (2024.alvr-1.15), described in WorldCuisines (arXiv 2410.12705) under 'Cultural VQA' related work as the dataset that 'specifically benchmarks the South East Asian region', built on UNESCO cultural-heritage imagery to test whether multimodal LLMs understand non-Western cultural context. He heads the VISTEC NLP group behind this line of Thai/SEA culture-specific LLM benchmarking, so the cultural-evaluation angle is a standing research direction rather than a one-off.

coauthors.name: Supasorn Suwajanakorn
coauthors.affiliation: Vidyasirimedhi Institute of Science and Technology (VISTEC), Thailand
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author of SEA-VQA, but his own research record is 3D computer vision and generative/neural rendering (face synthesis, novel-view synthesis) with no work on cultural values, cultural bias or value alignment in LLMs/NLP. Under the strict gate, the single shared culture-benchmark paper with the target is co-authorship rather than an independent cultural-values line of work, so marked not relevant.
